name: WRECK PROTOCOL: Behemoth Demolition Tournament
description: An annual two-week tournament held in the decommissioned Calumet Refinery complex, WRECK PROTOCOL pits custom-built autonomous machines — with a special open class for Iowan Behemoth-derived chassis — against each other and against a series of industrial obstacle gauntlets designed by the event's engineering collective, the Calumet Wreck Board. Unlike MACHINE WARS' year-round format, WRECK PROTOCOL is a singular event that draws machine crews from across the Great Lakes corridor, and its final-day 'Grand Demolition' — in which all surviving machines are simultaneously released into the same arena — has become a genuine cultural event. The tournament has no corponation sponsorship by charter and is funded entirely by entry fees and audience Quanta.
story_hooks: A Calumet Wreck Board member discovers that a machine entered in the open class contains components that are legally classified as restricted military hardware — and the entry form lists a shell company as owner.

A Tier 4 engineer who attends WRECK PROTOCOL anonymously every year finally enters a machine of her own design and finds that her corporate employer has taken notice — the machine contains proprietary logic she developed on company time.

The Calumet Wreck Board receives a legitimate offer of corponation sponsorship large enough to fund the event for a decade, and the community must decide whether their no-corporate charter is a principle or a luxury.
